articleTitle: Research in engineering, research in design research in engineering design. They're not one and the same thing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Research in Engineering Design
abstract: Not so many years ago, the transition from research output to products carried or necessitated few constraints other than technical function and thus was born the blurring of the edges and the confusion between research and design. The author works around the proposition that in modern day terms, engineering and engineering research is a valid, vital and necessary input to what is termed the 'totality of design'. Examples are given of products emerging from such research. The author examines the direction and re-direction of engineering research emanating from rigorous product design/process interaction and triggered by this process. It is to the effectiveness and efficiency of this process that the paper is devoted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Britain's need for better engineering design: a university researcher's viewpoint
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Research in Engineering Design
abstract: It is being increasingly recognised that one of the many reasons why Britain has lagged behind Japan, Germany and several other industrially-based nations in post-war years has been the fact that its products, processes and systems have simply not been good enough. The author examines the UK's need for better engineering design and gives three reasons for current inadequacies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Designing the design machine through crunching symbolic descriptions and inheritance hierarchies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Research in Engineering Design
abstract: The author introduces some of the basic principles that have led to the development of a distinctive computing mechanism, called SPLINTER, programmed by the author. SPLINTER is a knowledge description language based around the notion of reasoning by means of classification. It is an evolving apparatus which is suitable for use in empirical, real-world selection domains, where there are decisions to be made between numerous viable or 'approximately satisfactory' solutions. Their immediate goal is to demonstrate the practicality of the language in a small, restricted domain of choosing between polymeric materials. Beyond this, they see their language as developing important computational abstraction strategies, which constitute the fundamentals of designing a design machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Research in Engineering Design
abstract: It is important to improve the safety, reliability, performance and competitiveness of all the products and technical systems which surround us. Since engineering design teams fundamentally influence these factors, it is important to ensure that the design processes they use are in line with 'best practice'. The aim of engineering design research is to build up a coherent body of knowledge which defines 'best practice' for a particular context. The author shows that a pragmatic approach to planning an integrated engineering design research programme might be to start with some tentative statements on what is known about design in general, and from these to derive some questions to be answered about engineering design and engineering design research.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: What is research in engineering design?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Research in Engineering Design
abstract: The author argues that research in engineering design is a justified description of a sector of engineering research. Its distinguishing features are that the research programmes are largely initiated in response to, or inspired by, the needs of designers and manufacturers, to enable them to utilise the latest technology and scientific knowledge in advanced competitive designs. He shows that the outcome from 'research in design' projects, whether short-term or long-term, should not be restricted to new knowledge, published in scientific or technical journals, but should be communicated using information technology techniques to the designers as rapidly as possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Research in Engineering Design
abstract: It is more or less universally accepted that design is an activity of crucial importance to manufacturing, to wealth generation and to national prosperity. The author aims to encourage the development of educational opportunity which integrates different design activities in a context of marketability, and to further the understanding of the dynamics of the inter-relationship of differentiated forms of designing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
